## Loop

Truths about how the work loop fails rather than about the system —
what the review prompt is distilled from.

| Date | Finding | Status | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-10 | [A repointed item's head and its own dated section ask for different things](loop/2026.08.10-a-repointed-items-head-and-its-own-dated-section-ask-for-different-things.md) | closed | The session that repoints an item under a new ADR writes both the head and a dated section in one pass, and the two can disagree about what the user is asked for; nothing goes red, and the worker arbitrates alone. |
| 2026-08-09 | [The queue is partitioned by the directory a row was queued from, and the loop straddles two](loop/2026.08.09-the-queue-is-partitioned-by-the-directory-a-row-was-queued-from.md) | open | `list_queue` and `read_run_log` answer for the rows queued from the calling session's directory only, and this loop's rows are split between `antscihub-SIEVE-v3` and `antscihub-SIEVE-v3/docs/todo`. Runs still execute serially in one window, so every partitioned view is a strict undercount of a queue that is really one. Today that cost one whole run (02:07:28, a worker with nothing to take) and handed this review the wrong transcript. |
| 2026-08-09 | [An item's ruling can license a review past what the review prompt grants](loop/2026.08.09-an-items-ruling-can-license-a-review-past-what-the-review-prompt-grants.md) | open | `a-bands-axis-has-no-vocabulary-and-no-plot.md`'s ruling ends "The review that lands the mechanism mints the ADR", and the review prompt's enumerated powers are status, criterion, items, findings, indexes — not ADRs. Two documents disagreed about what this review could do, neither goes red, and the worker read the same sentence and correctly left the ADR undone. The review minted it anyway; that is a license flowing upward, which the standing rule says loop prompts never grant. |
| 2026-08-09 | [An item's clause that lands only in paintEvent is outside every oracle](loop/2026.08.09-an-items-clause-that-lands-only-in-paintevent-is-outside-every-oracle.md) | open | Three Phase 9 widgets have now closed green with a body clause whose only realization is a `paintEvent` call — the viewport badge, the strip's armed edges, and the crop fan's numbering and dimming. The idiom that makes the rest of these widgets testable, geometry exposed as a public method and paint left as its consequence, is what puts those clauses out of reach: the reviewer's clause-by-clause read marks them built because they are, and the mutation check is pointed at the geometry the cases already cover. |
| 2026-08-09 | [An item's alongside question is answered only in the run log](loop/2026.08.09-an-items-alongside-question-is-answered-only-in-the-run-log.md) | open | An item's "worth deciding alongside" clause cannot reach the criterion — the criterion witnesses the primary change — so a worker that rules "change nothing" leaves the ruling in its final message and the item closes `done` with the second question indistinguishable from dropped. The closing review is the last reader who still has the run log, which makes landing the ruling the review's job and not the worker's. |
| 2026-08-09 | [An invariant that only the rejected alternative breaks has no red to show](loop/2026.08.09-an-invariant-that-only-the-rejected-alternative-breaks-has-no-red-to-show.md) | open | 08.3's worker wrote a second case pinning "the same cut written twice replaces rather than accumulates" — the invariant that ruled the item's other shape out — then deleted it because it was green on the unchanged tree, reading the loop's red-before-green rule as forbidding it. It is not vacuous: it fails against the design the item rejected, so the discriminator the rule wants is whether a case can go red for a *plausible* implementation, not whether it went red for the *previous* one. |
| 2026-08-09 | [A subject-deferral's gate lifts and nothing in the repo notices](loop/2026.08.09-a-subject-deferrals-gate-lifts-and-nothing-in-the-repo-notices.md) | closed | Four items deferred_for subject on one gating item stayed deferred after that item landed. Nothing derives a gate's state — gated_on is prose, deferred is excluded from the queue by status alone, and doc_index validates the pair without ever asking whether the thing named has happened. The review of the gating item is the only session that holds both facts. |
| 2026-08-09 | [A review's partial-deferral note narrows the item on a prediction nothing checks](loop/2026.08.09-a-reviews-partial-deferral-note-narrows-the-item-on-a-prediction-nothing-checks.md) | closed | 09.7's review section told the work run which clauses waited on a deferred 09.2, and it was wrong about one of them: occlusion needs a fan-out, which schema v1 permits, not the fan-in it refuses. The worker re-derived the gate and built the clause. Had it trusted the note, the item would have closed green with a buildable clause unbuilt and nothing anywhere would have disagreed — a `-k` criterion is satisfied by the tests that exist. |

A GUI case asserting "the panel carries no stale mark after a dropped write" was red on the unfixed tree because the driving key never reached the widget and the window's own hotkey marked the panel instead — the same assertion, the same line, a cause the case does not mention — and it stayed red after the fix. Attribution needs a second observable that the defect moves and the artefact does not. |

The run built two, deferred the stage headers loudly into a new item with its own red criterion, and dropped the plots clause without naming it anywhere; the deferral is what made the omission invisible, because an account that argues one unbuilt clause at length reads as an account of everything unbuilt. |

Same visible failure, two mechanisms, two different remedies. |

A command that spawns a grandchild therefore runs to the grandchild's own completion before `TimeoutExpired` is raised: measured 40.1 s under a 3 s timeout for `uv run python -c "sleep(40)"`, which is the shape of every oracle the loop uses. The verdict is right and the bound is not there. |
